INSERT INTO news (title, slug, excerpt, categoryId, date, blocks, status, featured, publishedAt) VALUES
(
  'Making My SCR Debut: Million Dollar Quartet (2025)',
  'scr-debut-million-dollar-quartet-2025',
  'Scenic design debut at South Coast Repertory, co-designing Million Dollar Quartet on the Segerstrom Stage.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2025-08-29',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'I''m thrilled to announce my scenic design debut at South Coast Repertory, co-designing *Million Dollar Quartet* alongside Efren Delgadillo Jr. The show launches SCR''s 62nd season on September 13, 2025, playing through October on the Segerstrom Stage.\n\n*Million Dollar Quartet* is a high-energy musical based on the legendary jam session between Elvis Presley, Johnny Cash, Jerry Lee Lewis, and Carl Perkins—a rock ''n'' roll moment immortalized in history. Designing a set that captures the spontaneous, high-stakes energy of that session, with humor and intimacy, has been a thrilling challenge.\n\nCollaborating with this team at SCR feels like coming home. The level of craft, production value, and storytelling urgency is everything I''ve been working toward. I''m grateful to David Ivers, Suzanne Appel, Kim Martin-Cotten, James Moye, and everyone at SCR for trusting me with this creative opportunity.')
  ),
  'published',
  1,
  '2025-08-29'
),
(
  'Assisting Tom Buderwitz on The Play That Goes Wrong at Seattle Rep',
  'assisting-play-that-goes-wrong-seattle-rep',
  'Assisting longtime mentor Tom Buderwitz on the hysterical production of The Play That Goes Wrong at Seattle Rep.',
  @assistant_scenic_design_id,
  '2025-08-28',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'On August 28, 2025, I stepped into the world of professional comedy theatre at Seattle Rep, assisting my longtime mentor Tom Buderwitz on *The Play That Goes Wrong*. This production challenged us to design a set that literally falls apart on cue—requiring precision engineering disguised as theatrical chaos.\n\nWorking with Tom has been transformative throughout my career. His approach to scenic design balances technical rigor with playful creativity, and watching him navigate the unique demands of this show reinforced lessons I''ll carry forward into my own work.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2025-08-28'
),
(
  'Opening Night: How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying at OST',
  'how-to-succeed-okoboji-summer-theatre',
  'Fast-paced, detail-rich production closing the 67th season at Okoboji Summer Theatre.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2025-08-07',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', '*How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying* opened at Okoboji Summer Theatre, closing the 67th season with a fast-paced, detail-rich production. The show''s satirical take on corporate America demanded a set that could shift between office spaces, executive suites, and fantasy sequences with speed and clarity.\n\nThis production marked another milestone in my long relationship with OST—a company that has shaped my approach to theatrical storytelling and collaborative design.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2025-08-07'
),
(
  '40 Productions at Okoboji Summer Theatre',
  '40-productions-okoboji-summer-theatre',
  'Celebrating 40 productions and 15 seasons with Okoboji Summer Theatre.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2025-08-06',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'This summer marks my 40th production at Okoboji Summer Theatre—my 15th season with the company. Time has flown, and I''m grateful for the people who''ve been there every step of the way.\n\nOST has been a creative home where I''ve grown as a designer, collaborator, and storyteller. From intimate dramas to large-scale musicals, each production has taught me something new about craft, pace, and the power of live theatre.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2025-08-06'
),
(
  'Opening Night: Deathtrap at Okoboji Summer Theatre',
  'deathtrap-okoboji-summer-theatre',
  'Suspense, wit, and intricate staging—Deathtrap opens with praise for its detailed and beautiful set.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2025-08-01',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'Suspense, wit, and intricate staging—*Deathtrap* opened at Okoboji Summer Theatre with a review praising the set as "detailed and beautiful." The show''s twisting plot and meta-theatrical elements required a design that could support both realism and theatrical artifice.\n\nCreating a space that felt lived-in yet heightened the thriller''s tension was a rewarding challenge. The set needed to reveal character while hiding secrets—a balance that defines the best scenic design.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2025-08-01'
),
(
  'My Season as Scenic Designer for New Swan Shakespeare Festival (2025)',
  'new-swan-shakespeare-festival-2025',
  'Season Scenic Designer bringing All''s Well That Ends Well and Much Ado About Nothing to life in UCI''s outdoor theater.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2025-07-01',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'This summer, I''m honored to serve as the Season Scenic Designer for the New Swan Shakespeare Festival, bringing *All''s Well That Ends Well* and *Much Ado About Nothing* to life in UCI''s stunning outdoor theater.\n\nDesigning for outdoor performance presents unique challenges—working with natural light, weather, and the architecture of the space itself. The New Swan''s thrust stage and intimate audience relationship demand designs that feel both epic and accessible.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2025-07-01'
),
(
  'Fifth Season Assisting Jo Winiarski — Utah Shakespeare Festival',
  'fifth-season-utah-shakespeare-festival',
  'Fifth season assisting Jo Winiarski on The Importance of Being Earnest, A Gentleman''s Guide to Love and Murder, and Steel Magnolias.',
  @assistant_scenic_design_id,
  '2025-06-01',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'This summer marks my fifth season assisting Jo Winiarski at the Utah Shakespeare Festival. Tonight *The Importance of Being Earnest* opens, followed by *A Gentleman''s Guide to Love and Murder* and *Steel Magnolias*.\n\nWorking with Jo has been one of the most formative experiences of my career. Her attention to detail, collaborative spirit, and ability to balance artistic vision with practical execution continue to inspire my own approach to design.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2025-06-01'
),
(
  'Opening Night: Romero at University of Missouri',
  'romero-university-of-missouri',
  'World-premiere play directed by Dr. David Crespy exploring the life and legacy of Archbishop Óscar Romero.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2025-04-01',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'Tonight is opening night for *Romero*, a world-premiere play at the University of Missouri directed by Dr. David Crespy—and I''m proud to be its Scenic Designer.\n\nThe play explores the life and legacy of Archbishop Óscar Romero, whose commitment to social justice cost him his life. Designing for this story required a set that could move between intimate moments of faith and the public violence of political oppression. The challenge was to create a space that honored both the spiritual and political dimensions of Romero''s story.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2025-04-01'
),
(
  'Scenic Design for Okoboji Summer Theatre — Summer 2025 Season',
  'okoboji-summer-theatre-2025-season',
  'Designing Bell, Book and Candle, Deathtrap, and How to Succeed... at Okoboji Summer Theatre.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2025-04-01',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'Stoked to be designing *Bell, Book and Candle*, *Deathtrap*, and *How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying* at Okoboji Summer Theatre this summer, as part of the Conservatory''s immersive season.\n\nEach show presents unique design challenges—from the witchy mid-century apartment of *Bell, Book and Candle* to the thriller mechanics of *Deathtrap* to the corporate satire of *How to Succeed*. Summer stock demands efficiency, creativity, and collaboration at high speed.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2025-04-01'
),
(
  'Shut Up, Sherlock Praised in SLO Review',
  'shut-up-sherlock-slo-review',
  'SLO Review calls Shut Up, Sherlock a standing-ovation-worthy romp, recognizing the scenic design.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2025-02-01',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'SLO Review calls *Shut Up, Sherlock* "a standing-ovation-worthy romp," and I''m proud to see my scenic design recognized alongside a brilliant creative team.\n\nThe show''s comedic energy and rapid-fire pacing required a set that could support physical comedy while maintaining visual clarity. Creating a space that felt both grounded and heightened was key to the production''s success.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2025-02-01'
),
(
  'Guys on Ice Receives Praise in SLO Review',
  'guys-on-ice-slo-review',
  'SLO Review highlights the scenic design''s support of comedy and camaraderie in Guys on Ice.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2025-02-01',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'SLO Review calls *Guys on Ice* "warm and funny," with special recognition for how the scenic design supported the comedy and camaraderie at the heart of the show.\n\nDesigning for this intimate two-hander meant creating an ice fishing shack that felt authentic, lived-in, and capable of supporting the show''s gentle humor and emotional depth.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2025-02-01'
),
(
  'Freaky Friday at Okoboji Summer Theatre Receives Praise',
  'freaky-friday-okoboji-summer-theatre',
  'Spencer Daily Reporter highlights Freaky Friday at OST, recognizing the scenic design.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2024-07-01',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'The Spencer Daily Reporter highlighted *Freaky Friday* at OST, noting the success of the production and recognizing my work as scenic designer.\n\nThe show''s body-swap premise required a set that could support both domestic realism and theatrical transformation. Creating a space that felt like home while allowing for magical moments was a rewarding design challenge.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2024-07-01'
),
(
  '2024 Okoboji Summer Theatre Season – Scenic Designs Announced',
  'okoboji-summer-theatre-2024-season',
  'Designing Baskerville, Freaky Friday, Barefoot in the Park, and The Music Man at Okoboji Summer Theatre.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2024-04-01',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'This summer I''ll be scenic designing four productions at Okoboji Summer Theatre: *Baskerville*, *Freaky Friday*, *Barefoot in the Park*, and *The Music Man*.\n\nEach show presents unique design challenges—from the comedic mystery of *Baskerville* to the domestic comedy of *Barefoot in the Park* to the epic scale of *The Music Man*. Summer stock demands efficiency, creativity, and collaboration at high speed.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2024-04-01'

(
  'Joining United Scenic Artists, Local USA 829',
  'joining-united-scenic-artists-829',
  'Becoming a member of United Scenic Artists, Local USA 829—a milestone in my professional journey.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2023-06-02',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'On June 2, 2023, I became a member of United Scenic Artists, Local USA 829. This milestone marks an important step in my professional journey as a scenic and experiential designer, connecting me to a community that upholds the highest standards of artistry in our field.\n\nJoining USA 829 represents not just professional recognition, but a commitment to the craft and the community of designers who shape live performance.')
  ),
  'published',
  1,
  '2023-06-02'
),
(
  'Scenic Design for ¡Lotería: Game On! at Theatre SilCo',
  'loteria-game-on-theatre-silco',
  'Bringing a fantastical portal world to life in Theatre SilCo''s bilingual production.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2023-05-01',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'This spring, I teamed up with lighting designer Jesús López to bring a fantastical portal world to life in Theatre SilCo''s bilingual production *¡Lotería: Game On!*, as featured by UCI Humanities News.\n\nThe show''s magical realism demanded a design that could shift between the everyday and the extraordinary. Creating a space that honored both the cultural specificity of the story and its universal themes of family and identity was a rewarding challenge.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2023-05-01'
),
(
  'Assisting My First Off-Broadway Show — The Fears (April–May 2023)',
  'first-off-broadway-show-the-fears',
  'Assisting Jo Winiarski on my first Off-Broadway production—a transformative experience.',
  @assistant_scenic_design_id,
  '2023-05-01',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'In spring 2023, I had the opportunity to assist scenic designer Jo Winiarski on my first Off-Broadway production, *The Fears*. Experiencing the flow of a New York creative rehearsal—alongside Jo''s refined approach—was transformative.\n\nWorking Off-Broadway exposed me to a different pace and scale of production. The attention to detail, the collaborative intensity, and the proximity to the audience all shaped my understanding of what scenic design can achieve.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2023-05-01'
),
(
  'Forum at Theatre SilCo Featured in Summit Daily',
  'forum-theatre-silco-summit-daily',
  'Summit Daily profiles A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum, spotlighting the scenic design.',
  @scenic_design_id,
  '2022-06-01',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'The Summit Daily profiled our production of *A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum*, spotlighting how the scenic design shaped the playful world of ancient Rome.\n\nThe show''s farcical energy and rapid-fire pacing required a set that could support physical comedy while maintaining visual clarity. Creating a space that felt both grounded in Roman architecture and heightened for comedy was key to the production''s success.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2022-06-01'
),
(
  'Stephens College Update — Looking Ahead to Spring 2022',
  'stephens-college-spring-2022',
  'First semester at Stephens complete—preparing for spring courses and scenic design work.',
  @academia_id,
  '2021-12-20',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'My first semester at Stephens flew by. As I prep for spring, I''m diving into new courses and scenic design work on *The Bald Soprano* and *Curtain Up!*\n\nTeaching scenic design has deepened my own practice. Articulating design principles, guiding students through the creative process, and watching them discover their own voices has been one of the most rewarding aspects of academia.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2021-12-20'
),
(
  'Returning to Stephens College as Assistant Professor of Scenic Design',
  'returning-stephens-college-assistant-professor',
  'Joining Stephens College as Assistant Professor of Scenic Design—returning to my hometown and alma mater.',
  @academia_id,
  '2021-08-07',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'I''ve joined Stephens College as Assistant Professor of Scenic Design. Returning to Columbia, MO—my hometown and undergrad alma mater—makes this a special milestone.\n\nTeaching at Stephens allows me to share what I''ve learned while continuing to grow as a designer. The opportunity to mentor emerging designers and contribute to the next generation of theatrical artists is both humbling and exciting.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2021-08-07'
),
(
  'Scenic Design for Lysistrata at UTEP — Spring 2021',
  'lysistrata-utep-spring-2021',
  'First in-person production since the pandemic began, adapting the design process with new COVID protocols.',
  @academia_id,
  '2021-04-15',
  JSON_ARRAY(
    JSON_OBJECT('type', 'text', 'content', 'I designed *Lysistrata* at UTEP in Spring 2021—my first in-person production since the pandemic began. Adapting the design process with new COVID protocols challenged us to rethink collaboration, safety, and the role of live performance.\n\nThe experience reinforced the resilience of theatre and the importance of creative problem-solving. Designing in a pandemic meant balancing artistic vision with practical constraints—a lesson that will shape my work for years to come.')
  ),
  'published',
  0,
  '2021-04-15'
);
